executionHistory.summary: Security round over the surface the five bug packets changed, derived from each packet's own commits rather than inherited; for this packet it is rltaxclaimage.js, rltaxsocialsecurity.js, tax-rules/benefit/2026.json and lifetime-tax-strategy-lab.html. ONE FINDING IS RECORDED AGAINST THIS PACKET, F-SEC-02, severity medium, not fixed here by design. The below-earliest-age refusal this packet shipped is PACK-RELATIVE, not absolute: rltaxsocialsecurity.js:571-598 admits earlyReductionRule.earliestClaimAge.ageYears on a Number.isFinite test alone, with no floor and no cross-check, so the pack decides its own bound. Separately, earliestClaimAge.maximumReductionMonths is read at line 618 only to push a comparisonRecord; nothing acts on its boolean, so the declared maximum bounds nothing. Executed against the shipped pack through the real module, PIA 2000, birth year 1960: claim at 744 months settles at 1400 and claim at 720 months REFUSES RLTAX-THRESHOLD-UNAVAILABLE, which is this packet's fix working; but with ageYears set to 20 a claim at 240 months SETTLES at monthly -2801 over 564 counted reduction months, and with ageYears set to 0 or -5 a claim at 0 months SETTLES at monthly -4801 over 804 months. With maximumReductionMonths set to 1 against 60 counted months the figure still settles unchanged at 1400, which is the executed proof that the declared maximum is inert. A negative monthly benefit is finite, so BUG-020's RLTAX-FIGURE-UNREPRESENTABLE guard at rltax.js:179 and rltax.js:1204 tests only Number.isFinite and does not catch it: the misleading figure reaches display as SETTLED rather than as a refusal, which is the same failure class this packet and BUG-020 were filed for.
